The temporal association with micturition is highly characteristic of micturition syncope — a reflex-mediated vasovagal syncope triggered by parasympathetic activation and sympathetic withdrawal during or immediately after voiding, especially in the setting of nocturnal urination, standing up quickly, or volume depletion (though not overtly present here). Contributing factors may include mild orthostatic stress (e.g., rising from sitting/lying to void at night), vagal stimulation from bladder emptying, and possibly mild vasodilation. The absence of structural heart disease, arrhythmia on ECG, neurological deficits, or seizure stigmata makes other causes (e.g., arrhythmic syncope, epilepsy, stroke, hypoglycemia, structural CNS pathology) much less likely. Orthostatic vital signs were not reported, but the clinical context strongly favors a neurally mediated reflex syncope subtype — specifically micturition syncope — which is a well-recognized variant of vasovagal syncope.

DIAGNOSIS: Micturition syncope
